evidence.summary: With K=64, group_size=32 (exact multiple) the kernel matches the contract reference to max_abs_err 4.8e-6 (rel 2.9e-7), showing the dequant convention (zero+1, scale, packing) is otherwise correct. With K=48, group_size=32 and 2 supplied scale/zero rows (exactly the ceil(K/group_size) supply the contract describes), the kernel deviates from the contract reference by max_abs_err 9.256 on ref_absmax 14.25 (rel 0.65), while matching a floor-clamp reference (g_idx = clamp(k//gs, max=K//gs-1)) to 2.9e-6. This is direct confirmation that trailing columns k>=32 are dequantized with group 0's scale/zero instead of their own group-1 row.

rationale: kernel.py lines 69-73 use floor division for num_groups and clamp; contract text explicitly requires ceil(K/group_size) rows and that trailing columns form their own group.

scope_evidence.summary: "every column must be dequantized with the scale and zero-point of the group it actually belongs to, for any K -- including a K that is not an exact multiple of group_size... scales and zeros are supplied with ceil(K / group_size) rows accordingly."
num_groups = K // group_size; g_idx = clamp(arange(K)//group_size, max=num_groups-1) -- floor instead of ceil.

scope_rationale: The contract paragraph is explicit that correctness must hold "for any K -- including a K that is not an exact multiple of group_size", and states scales/zeros are supplied with ceil(K/group_size) rows. So K=48, group_size=32 with 2 scale/zero rows is an admitted input.
statement: The host wrapper's group table uses num_groups = K // group_size and clamps g_idx to num_groups-1, so when K is not an exact multiple of group_size the trailing columns are dequantized with the previous group's scale/zero instead of their own final-group row, violating the stated contract (which requires ceil(K/group_size) groups).
